column1: # Things a lowercase, letters-only dictionary cannot spell on its own: dropped
# apostrophes, the pronoun "I", and abbreviations whose dots would end the
# A dropped apostrophe is a typographic shortcut, not a spelling mistake, so
# the contraction has to be right there.  Where the input is *also* a real word
# ("its", "were", "ill", "cant", "lets") that word rightly comes first and the
# "i" is different again: it has no valid lowercase form, so the corpus entry
# Two-letter input that is not itself a word leads with the literal, because
# "cm", "ms" and "CW" are units and acronyms far more often than abbreviations
# -- so "im" costs one extra slot here.  See tests/cases/literal.tsv.
